records.arabic: اليشكري تقدم في الأول
records.english: Al-Yashkuri; he was mentioned in the first section.

heading.english: The letter sin followed by lam

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الحضرمي سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم روى عنه عمرو بن ربيعة ذكره هكذا البخاري وتبعه بن عدي وقال لا يعرف واستدركه مغلطاي في كتابه الإمامة وهو خطأ نشأ عن تصحيف في اسم أبيه والصواب قيصر وقد تبدل الصاد سينا وقد قيل في اسمه هو سلامة بزيادة هاء وقد تقدم ذكره في رواية عمرو بن ربيعة في الأول
records.english: Al-Hadrami heard the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. Amr ibn Rabi'ah transmitted from him. Al-Bukhari mentioned him thus, and Ibn Adi followed him and said: He is not known. Mughaltay added him in his book al-Imama. This is an error arising from a misreading of his father's name. The correct form is Qaysar; the sad was changed to a sin. It has also been said that his name is Salama, with an additional ha. He was previously mentioned in the narration of Amr ibn Rabi'a in the first section.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: فرق بعضهم بينه وبين سلمان الفارسي وهو هو ونبه على ذلك بن حبان
records.english: Some distinguished him from Salman al-Farisi, but he is the same man. Ibn Hibban pointed this out.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: جد عبد الحميد بن يزيد بن سلمة غاير بينه وبين سلمة بن يزيد وهما واحد
records.english: The grandfather of Abd al-Hamid ibn Yazid ibn Salamah. A distinction was made between him and Salama ibn Yazid, but they are one person.

names.arabic: عبد الحميد بن يزيد بن سلمة
names.english: Abd al-Hamid ibn Yazid ibn Salama

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الجرمي أفرده بعضهم وأورده فيمن اسمه سلمة بفتح اللام وهو وهم على وهم فإنه بكسر اللام وهو والد عمرو واسم أبيه قيس على الصحيح وقد تقدم على الصواب في الأول وأن بعضهم وحد بينه وبين سلمة بن نفيع والراجح التعدد
records.english: Al-Jarmi; some listed him separately and included him among those named Salamah. They gave the lam a fatha. This is error upon error: it has a kasra on the lam. He is Amr's father, and his own father's name, according to the sounder view, is Qays. He was previously mentioned correctly in the first section, along with the fact that some identified him with Salama ibn Nufay', whereas the stronger view is that they are two people. The name is also rendered “Salima ibn Abi Salima al-Jarmi.”

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: فرق أبو يعلى بينه وبين سلمة بن المحبق وتبعه أبو نعيم وكذا هو في مسند بقي بن مخلد وعلم له الذهبي علامة بقي بن مخلد فإنه أخرج له حديثين وكل ذلك وهم فإنهما واحد وقد نبه على ذلك أبو موسى فأصاب
records.english: Abu Ya'la distinguished him from Salamah ibn al-Muhabbiq, and Abu Nu'aym followed him. He is likewise treated this way in Baqi ibn Makhlad's Musnad, and al-Dhahabi assigned him Baqi ibn Makhlad's mark, for the latter included two hadiths for him. All of this is an error: the two are one person. Abu Musa pointed this out and was right. The name is also rendered “Salama al-Hudhali.”

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ذكره بن شاهين مختصرا وقال أن لهم مسجدا بالكوفة وتبعه أبو موسى ولم يتعقبه وهو وهم نشأ عن تصحيف وإنما هم سلمة المجر جد سمرة بن معاوية بن عمرو بن سلمة الماضي في القسم الأول وكان سلمة المذكور قبل الإسلام والمجر بالجيم بغير موحدة كما تقدم
records.english: Ibn Shahin mentioned him briefly and said that they had a mosque in Kufa. Abu Musa followed him without challenging him. This is an error caused by a misreading. The intended identification is Salama al-Majar, the grandfather of Samura ibn Mu'awiya ibn Amr ibn Salama, mentioned earlier in the first section. The source unexpectedly uses a plural pronoun before the singular name. That Salama lived before Islam. Al-Majar is written with a jim and without a ba, as already noted.

names.arabic: سمرة بن معاوية بن عمرو بن سلمة
names.english: Samura ibn Mu'awiya ibn Amr ibn Salama

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وعنه يزيد بن أبي حبيب قال أبو عمر حديثه عندي مرسل قلت لم أر من ذكره في الصحابة قبله بل قال بن أبي حاتم روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مرسلا وذكره بن حبان في ثقات التابعين وأنه روى عن أنس ثم انني رأيت في عدة نسخ من الاستيعاب أن اسم أبيه ندير بالنون والذال مصغرا وآخره راء والمعروف فيه إنما هو يزيد بالتحتانية والزاي وآخره دال بغير تصغير
records.english: He related from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, and Yazid ibn Abi Habib related from him. Abu Umar said: 'In my view, his hadith is mursal.' I say: I have not seen anyone before him include this man among the Companions. Rather, Ibn Abi Hatim said that he narrated from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم in a mursal report. Ibn Hibban listed him among the trustworthy Successors and said that he narrated from Anas. Later I saw, in several copies of al-Isti'ab, that his father's name was written as Nudayr, in the diminutive and ending in ra. The canonical text nevertheless describes its second consonant as dhal, at odds with the written dal; the intended reading remains uncertain. The name known for his father, however, is Yazid, beginning with ya and containing zay, and ending with dal, without a diminutive.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: خادم للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذكره بن شاهين وتبعه أبو موسى فأخرج من طريق جعفر الصادق عن أبيه عن سلمى خادم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن أزواج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كن يجعلن رءوسهن أربعة قرون فإذا اغتسلن جمعنها الحديث وسلمى امرأة وهي أم رافع زوجة أبي رافع فظن أن قوله خادم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم رجلا وليس كذلك وذكر بن شاهين وأبو موسى من طريقه أن الراوي قال مرة في هذا الحديث عن سالم خادم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فكأنه تغير من سلمى والله أعلم
records.english: A servant of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم; Ibn Shahin mentioned her. Abu Musa followed him. He transmitted, through Ja'far al-Sadiq, from his father, from Salma, the servant of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, that the wives of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم used to arrange their hair in four locks, and when they bathed they gathered them together, and the rest of the hadith. Salma is a woman: she is Umm Rafi', the wife of Abu Rafi'. Someone supposed that the description 'servant of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم' referred to a man, but it did not. Ibn Shahin, and Abu Musa through him, also related that the transmitter once said in this hadith, 'from Salim, servant of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم.' It seems to have been altered from Salma. والله أعلم

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن مالك بن حسل العامري أفرده الطبراني ومن تبعه عن سليط بن عمرو بن عبد شمس وهو هو فعمرو والده هو بن عبد شمس بن عبد ود بن نصر بن مالك فنسب إلى جد أبيه فظنوه آخر ولكن القصة واحدة وهو كونه كان الرسول إلى هوذة بن علي
records.english: Son of Malik ibn Hisl, al-Amiri. Al-Tabarani and those who followed him listed him separately from Sulayt ibn Amr ibn Abd Shams, but they are the same man. His father Amr was the son of Abd Shams ibn Abd Wudd ibn Nasr ibn Malik. The source says Sulayt was attributed to 'his father's grandfather,' so they supposed him to be another person; the stated lineage places Malik further back than that description suggests. The story is the same: he was the envoy to Hawdha ibn Ali.

aliases: Sulayt ibn Amr ibn Abd Shams
names.arabic: سليط بن عمرو بن مالك بن حسل العامري
names.english: Sulayt ibn Amr ibn Malik ibn Hisl al-Amiri

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ينظر من القسم الأول فقد جزم بن منده وابن ماكولا بأنه وهم وأن الصواب أبو السليل الذي يروي عن أبي المليح
records.english: Consult the first section; Ibn Mandah stated this categorically. Ibn Makula also stated decisively that this is an error and that the correct name is Abu al-Salil, who narrates from Abu al-Malih.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: قال الحاكم في علوم الحديث أدخله على بن سعيد العسكري وغيره في الصحابة وأخرج من طريق زهير بن محمد عن عثمان بن سليمان عن أبيه أنه سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ في المغرب بالطور قال الحاكم وهذا معلوم من ثلاثة أوجه أحدها أن عثمان إنما هو بن أبي سليمان وأبو سليمان هو بن محمد بن جبير بن مطعم فليس لأبيه صحبة ثانيها أن عثمان إنما رواه عن نافع بن جبير عن أبيه فسقط نافع بن جبير ثالثها أن سليمان لم يسمع من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قلت الثالث نتيجة ما قبله
records.english: Al-Hakim said in The Sciences of Hadith that Ali ibn Sa'id al-Askari included him. Others also included him among the Companions. He transmitted through Zuhayr ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Sulayman, from his father, that he heard the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم recite Surat al-Tur at the sunset prayer. Al-Hakim said: This is known to be erroneous in three ways. First, Uthman is actually Ibn Abi Sulayman, and Abu Sulayman is the son of Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im; thus his father was not a Companion. Second, Uthman actually narrated it from Nafi' ibn Jubayr, from his father, but Nafi' ibn Jubayr was dropped from the chain. Third, Sulayman did not hear from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. I say: The third point follows from those before it.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: وقع حديثه في معجم بن الأعرابي من رواية قرة عن سليمان بن جابر قال أتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وعليه بردة وإن هدبها لعلي قدميه فقلت أوصني فقال لا تحقرن من المعروف شيئا الحديث وقرأت بخط مغلطاي أن بن منده أورده في تاريخه في ترجمة محمد بن الصلت بن غالب الهجيمي قلت وسليمان هذا صوابه سليم وهو أبو جرى الهجيمي وسليمان تصحيف
records.english: His report occurs in Ibn al-A'rabi's Mu'jam through Qurrah's transmission. In that narration, Sulayman ibn Jabir said: I came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم while he was wearing a cloak whose fringes reached down over his feet. I said, 'Counsel me.' He replied, 'Do not consider any good deed too small,' and the rest of the hadith. I read in Mughaltay's handwriting that Ibn Manda included him in his History under the biography of Muhammad ibn al-Salt ibn Ghalib al-Hujaymi. I say: The correct name for this Sulayman is Sulaym. He is Abu Jari al-Hujaymi, and 'Sulayman' is a misreading. The name is also rendered “Ibn al-Arabi.”

names.arabic: محمد بن الصلت بن غالب الهجيمي
names.english: Muhammad ibn al-Salt ibn Ghalib al-Hujaymi

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: تابعي أرسل حديثا فذكره بعضهم في الصحابة قال بن أبي حاتم روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مرسلا روى عنه موسى بن أبي عائشة
records.english: A Successor who transmitted a report without naming an intermediary. The chain omitted a Companion, so some included him among the Companions. Ibn Abi Hatim said: He narrated from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم in a mursal report; Musa ibn Abi A'isha narrated from him.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ذكره الطبري في الصحابة وهو وهم فروى بن منده من طريق أبي حريز أن رفاعة حدثه أن صاحبا له قال له انطلق بنا إلى المختار فإنه يدعو إلى نصرة آل محمد فدخلنا عليه قال فذكر كلمة فأهويت إلى قائم السيف فذكرت كلمة سليمان بن مسهر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال إذا ائتمنك رجل على دمه فلا تقتله قال بن منده هذا وهم والصواب عن رفاعة عن عمرو بن المحبق قلت الذي يظهر أن أبا حريز وهم في اسم والد سليمان بن صرد فإن الحديث رواه بن أبي ليلى عن أبي عكاشة عن رفاعة عن سليمان بن صرد فإن كان أبو حريز حفظ فيه سليمان بن مسهر فيكون من رواية تابعي عن تابعي فإن رفاعة تابعي وسليمان بن مسهر تابعي أيضا مشهور في تابعي أهل الكوفة والمتن معروف من رواية رفاعة عن عمرو بن المحبق كما قال بن منده أخرجه النسائي وابن ماجة وقد ذكرته من طريق أبي حريز في ترجمة المختار مطولا
records.english: Al-Tabari listed him among the Companions, but this is an error. Ibn Manda narrated through Abu Hariz that Rifa'a told him that a companion of his said to him, 'Come with us to al-Mukhtar, for he calls people to support the family of Muhammad.' We went in to him. The account continues with an unspecified statement; its narrator reached for the hilt of his sword and then recalled a saying of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم reported by Sulayman ibn Mushir: 'If a man entrusts you with his life, do not kill him.' The report does not identify who uttered that statement. Ibn Manda said: This is an error; the correct chain is from Rifa'a, from Amr ibn al-Muhabbiq. I say: It appears that Abu Hariz erred in the name of the father of Sulayman ibn Surad, for Ibn Abi Layla narrated this hadith from Abu Ukkasha, from Rifa'a, from Sulayman ibn Surad. If Abu Hariz did preserve the name Sulayman ibn Mushir, the report would be a Successor narrating from a Successor: Rifa'a is a Successor, and Sulayman ibn Mushir is also a Successor, well known among the Successors of Kufa. The text of the hadith is known in a narration from Rifa'a, from Amr ibn al-Muhabbiq, as Ibn Manda said; al-Nasa'i and Ibn Maja included it. I quoted it at greater length through Abu Hariz in the biography of al-Mukhtar.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: غير منسوب استدركه بن فتحون وهو وهم نشأ عن تصحيف فأخرج بإسناده من طريق بن عيينة عن إسحاق بن أبي طلحة أنه سمع أنس بن مالك يقول صليت أنا وسليم في بيتنا خلف رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وصلت أمي من ورائنا هكذا أخرجه من جزء يحيى بن يحيى النيسابوري المشهور عن بن عيينة والحديث في الجزء المذكور على الصواب بلفظ صليت أنا ويتيم كذا أخرجه البخاري من رواية بن عيينة وقد قيل أن اسم اليتيم المذكور ضميرة
records.english: No lineage is given. Ibn Fathun added him. This is an error caused by a misreading. He transmitted with his chain through Ibn Uyayna, from Ishaq ibn Abi Talha, who heard Anas ibn Malik say: 'Sulaym and I prayed in our house behind the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم, and my mother prayed behind us.' This is how he transmitted it from the well-known collection of Yahya ibn Yahya al-Naysaburi, from Ibn Uyayna. But the hadith in that collection correctly reads, 'I and an orphan prayed'; al-Bukhari likewise transmitted it from Ibn Uyayna. It has been said that the orphan's name was Dumayra.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ذكره الخطيب في المؤتلف من طريق محمد بن هارون بن حميد المجدر عن الحسن بن شاذان الواسطي قال حدثنا أبو عاصم حدثنا أبو نعامة العدوي عن عبد العزيز بن بشير عن سليم الضبي قال قلت يا رسول الله إن أبي كان يقري الضيف ويفعل كذا الأشياء عدها فقال أدرك الإسلام قلت لا قال ليس بنافعه فلما رأى ما بي قال أنه لا يزال ذلك في عقبة لا يظلمون ولا يستذلون ولا يفتقرون قال الخطيب كذا قال وإنما هو سلمان قلت هو بن عامر الضبي الصحابي المشهور كذا أخرجه الطبراني والحاكم والدارقطني والخطيب في المؤتلف من طرق عن أبي عاصم عن أبي نعامة عن عبد العزيز بن بشير عن جده سلمان بن عامر الضبي وهو الصواب
records.english: Al-Khatib mentioned him in Al-Mu'talif. The report came through Muhammad ibn Harun ibn Humayd al-Mujaddar, from al-Hasan ibn Shadhan al-Wasiti, who said: Abu Asim told us, from Abu Nu'ama al-Adawi, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Bashir, from Sulaym al-Dabbi, who said: I said, 'Messenger of God, my father used to entertain guests and do such-and-such things,' and he enumerated them. The Prophet asked, 'Did he live to see Islam?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'Then it does not benefit him.' When he saw my distress, he said, 'That will continue among his descendants: they will not be wronged, humiliated, or impoverished.' Al-Khatib said: He stated it thus, but the name is actually Salman. I say: He is the well-known Companion Salman ibn Amir al-Dabbi. Al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, al-Daraqutni, and al-Khatib in al-Mu'talif all transmitted it through various routes from Abu Asim, from Abu Nu'ama, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Bashir, from his grandfather Salman ibn Amir al-Dabbi. This is correct.

names.arabic: محمد بن هارون بن حميد المجدر
names.english: Muhammad ibn Harun ibn Humayd al-Mujaddar

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الأنصاري الزرقي قال بن عساكر أدرك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وخرج إلى الشام غازيا وقال الواقدي كان يحمل لواء شرحبيل بن حسنة قلت هكذا استدركه مغلطاي وحرف اسم والده وإنما هو خلدة كما تقدم في القسم الأول
records.english: Al-Ansari al-Zuraqi; Ibn Asakir said that he lived in the time of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. He also went out to Syria on campaign. Al-Waqidi said that he carried the banner of Shurahbil ibn Hasana. I say: Mughaltay added him in this form but distorted his father's name. It is actually Khalda, as previously stated in the first section.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: مصغرا بن عامر الخبائري تابعي استدركه مغلطاي وقال روى شعبة عن يزيد بن حمير سمعت سليم بن عامر وكان قد أدرك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال بن عساكر ورواية من روى وكان أدرك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أصح قلت ما رأيت هذا الذي نقله عن بن عساكر في ترجمة سليم من تاريخه بل ذكر الرواية التي فيها أدرك أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقط نعم ذكر ذلك المزي في ترجمته لكن عبر بالصحيح وهو الصواب فإن سليم بن عامر هذا تابعي مشهور ذكره بن سعد في الطبقة الثالثة قال وكان ثقة قديما وقال بن معين في تاريخه كان يقول استقبلت الإسلام من أوله وزعم أنه قرئ عليه كتاب عمر ومراده بقوله استقبلت إلى آخره المبالغة في ادراكه أيام الفتوح وحضوره كتاب عمر يجوز أن يكون وهو صغير فقد قال أبو حاتم في المراسيل روى عن عوف بن مالك مرسلا ولم يدرك المقداد بن الأسود ولا عمرو بن عبسة وأرخوا وفاته سنة ثلاثين وقد تقرر عند أهل الحديث أنه لم يبق أحد من الناس على رأس المائة من يوم قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل وفاته بشهر لا يبقى على الأرض ممن هو عليها اليوم أحد فكان آخر من ضبطت وفاته ممن رأى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أبو الطفيل عامر بن وائلة واختلف في سنة وفاته فأنهى ما قيل فيها سنة عشر ومائة وذلك عند تكملة المائة سواء فظهر أن قول من قال في الرواية المذكورة إنه أدرك أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم هو الصواب والله أعلم
records.english: In the diminutive form, son of Amir al-Khaba'iri. He was a Successor. Mughaltay added him and said: Shu'ba narrated from Yazid ibn Humayr, who said, 'I heard Sulaym ibn Amir, and he had encountered the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم.' Ibn Asakir said: The narration of those who report 'and he had encountered the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم' is more sound. I say: I have not seen what he attributes to Ibn Asakir in Sulaym's biography in the latter's History. Rather, Ibn Asakir gave only the version saying, 'He encountered the Companions of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم.' Al-Mizzi did mention that in his biography, but used the expression 'the sound version,' and that is correct. This Sulaym ibn Amir is a well-known Successor. Ibn Sa'd listed him in the third class and said that he was trustworthy from early on. Ibn Ma'in said in his History that Sulaym used to say, 'I experienced Islam from its beginning,' and claimed that Umar's letter was read to him. By 'I experienced...' he meant to emphasize that he witnessed the days of the conquests. He may have been a child when Umar's letter was read to him. Abu Hatim said in al-Marasil that his narration from Awf ibn Malik is mursal, and that he did not encounter al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad or Amr ibn Abasa. They dated his death to 'the year thirty'; the source does not give a century, and this date is difficult to reconcile with the chronology that follows. Hadith scholars have established that one hundred years after the day, a month before his death, when the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم said, 'Of those on the earth today, not one will remain on the earth,' no one was left. The last person whose death was recorded among those who saw the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم was Abu al-Tufayl Amir ibn Wa'ila. The year of his death is disputed; the latest year given is one hundred and ten, precisely at the completion of that century. Thus the correct version is the one saying that Sulaym encountered the Companions of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. The name is also rendered “Sulaym, in the diminutive, ibn Amir al-Khaba'iri.” والله أعلم

names.english: Sulaym, in the diminutive, ibn Amir al-Khaba'iri

records.arabic: ينظر من القسم الأول وقد ذكر فيه أن أبا موسى أشار إلى أنه وهو وأن الصواب قصة ماعز مع هزال التي ستأتي في حرف الهاء
records.english: Consult the first section; he was mentioned there. Abu Musa indicated this was an error and that the correct reference is to the story of Ma'iz with Hazzal, which will appear under the letter ha. The canonical clause describing Abu Musa's judgment is damaged; the sense 'an error' follows a variant reading.

records.arabic: أحد التسعة من بني عبس ذكره الطبري وغيره وهكذا استدركه بن فتحون وكذا رأيته في التجريد للذهبي وهو وهو نشأ عن تصحيف والصواب سباع بكسر المهملة ثم موحدة خفيفة وآخره عين
records.english: One of the nine men of Banu Abs; al-Tabari and others mentioned him. Ibn Fathun added him in this form, and I likewise saw him in al-Dhahabi's al-Tajrid. This is an error arising from a misreading. The correct name is Siba', with a kasra on the unpointed first letter, then a single ba, and ending in ayn.

heading.english: The letter sin followed by nun

records.arabic: كذا ذكره بعضهم والصواب سيار بتحتانية وآخره راء
records.english: This is how some mentioned him, but the correct form is Sayyar. The name is written with a ya and a final ra.

records.arabic: وقع ذكره في الأحياء للغزالي في أواخر كتاب الفقر والزهد من الربع الأخير وهو ربع المنجيات قال فيه وعن سنان بن سعد قال حيكت للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وجبة من صوف وجعلت حاشيتها سوداء فلما لبسها قال انظروا ما أحسنها وما لبسها فقام إليه أعرابي فقال يا رسول الله هبها لي قال وكان إذا سئل شيئا لم يبخل به فدفعها إليه وأمر أن تحاك له جبة أخرى فمات وهي في المحاكة قال شيخنا في تخريجه هذا الحديث أخرجه الطيالسي والطبراني من حديث سهل بن سعد وهو عند الطبراني بالقصة الأخيرة ووقع في كثير من نسخ الأحياء سنان بن سعد وهو غلط والله أعلم
records.english: He is mentioned in al-Ghazali's Ihya', near the end of the book on poverty and renunciation. This was in the last quarter, the Quarter of the Saving Virtues. It says: From Sinan ibn Sa'd, who said, 'A woolen robe was woven for the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, with a black border. When he put it on, he said, "Look how fine it is!" The text then says that he had not worn it, although it has just said he put it on. A Bedouin came up to him and said, "Messenger of God, give it to me." When he was asked for something, he did not withhold it, so he gave it to him and ordered another robe to be woven for him. He died while it was still being woven.' Our shaykh said in his sourcing of this hadith: Al-Tayalisi and al-Tabarani transmitted it as a hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd; in al-Tabarani it includes the final part of the story. Many copies of al-Ihya read 'Sinan ibn Sa'd,' which is an error. والله أعلم

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: أورده بن شاهين وأورد له حديثين من رواية سلمة بن جنادة عنه وافرده عن سنان بن المحبق وهو وهم وسنان له رؤية لا سماع وقد خبط فيه أبو عمر فقال سنان بن سلمة الأسلمي بصري روى عنه قتادة ومعاذ بن سعد في حديثه اضطراب قلت فوهم في نسبه وإنما هو هذلي وقد بين البغوي سبب الوهم وأن بعض الرواة توهم صحبته من إرسال الحديث فأخرج من طريق بن أبي ليلى عن عبد الكريم بن أبي المخارق عن معاذ بن سعد عن سنان بن سلمة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعث ببدنتين مع رجل الحديث قال ورواه بن جريج عن عبد الكريم عن معاذ بن سعد عن سنان بن سلمة عن أبيه وكانت له صحبة فذكره وهذا هو الصواب وقد تقدم شيء منه في القسم الثاني
records.english: Ibn Shahin included him and cited two reports about him. The reports came through Salama ibn Junada. He treated him separately from Sinan ibn al-Muhabbiq, which is an error. Sinan saw the Prophet but did not hear him. Abu Umar became confused about him, saying, 'Sinan ibn Salama al-Aslami, a Basran. Qatada and Mu'adh ibn Sa'd narrated from him. His hadith is confused.' I say: He erred about his tribal attribution; the man was actually a Hudhali. Al-Baghawi explained the cause of the error: some narrators assumed that Sinan was a Companion because the hadith was transmitted without its intervening link. He transmitted through Ibn Abi Layla, from Abd al-Karim ibn Abi al-Mukhariq, from Mu'adh ibn Sa'd, from Sinan ibn Salama, that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم sent two sacrificial camels with a man, and the rest of the hadith. Al-Baghawi said: Ibn Jurayj narrated it from Abd al-Karim, from Mu'adh ibn Sa'd, from Sinan ibn Salama, from his father, who was a Companion, and then gave the account. This is correct. Part of this was previously given in the second section.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: استدركه أبو موسى وأورد من طريق بن لهيعة عن يزيد عن أبي الخير عن سندر رفعه أسلم سالمها الله الحديث وفيه تجيب أجابت قلت قد ذكره بن منده فلا يستدرك وكأن أبا موسى لما رآه في هذه الرواية كنى أبا الأسود ظنه آخر وليس كذلك فإنه كنيته أبو الأسود وله ولد اسمه عبد الله كنى به أيضا وسيأتي فيمن اسمه عبد الله
records.english: Abu Musa added him and cited a report through Ibn Lahi'ah. The chain continued from Yazid, from Abu al-Khayr, from Sindar, with a report raised to the Prophet: 'Aslam—may God keep her safe,' and the rest of the hadith, in which it says, 'Tujib responded.' I say: Ibn Manda already mentioned him, so he should not be added. It seems that when Abu Musa saw him bearing the kunya Abu al-Aswad in this narration, he thought him to be someone else. He is not: Abu al-Aswad is his kunya. He also had a son named Abd Allah, after whom he was likewise given a kunya. This will appear among those named Abd Allah.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن جزء الزبيدي روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في النهي عن استقبال القبلة للبول رواه الليث عنه عنه قاله البخاري هكذا استدركه بن فتحون فغلط غلطا شنيعا وإنما قال البخاري سهل بن ثعلبة عن بن جزء فسقط عن وكيف يتخيل بن فتحون أن الليث يروي عن صحابي وقد أخرج الحديث الطبراني من طريق سهل عن عبد الله بن الحارث بن جزء وسهل معدود في التابعين عند البخاري وأبي حاتم وكل من ذكره
records.english: Son of Juz', al-Zubaydi. He narrated from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم concerning the prohibition on facing the qibla when urinating. Al-Layth narrated it from him, as al-Bukhari stated; the canonical text repeats 'from him' here, leaving the link unclear. Ibn Fathun added him in this form, committing a grave error. Al-Bukhari actually said, 'Sahl ibn Tha'laba, from Ibn Juz',' but the word 'from' was dropped. How could Ibn Fathun imagine that al-Layth narrated directly from a Companion? Al-Tabarani transmitted the hadith through Sahl, from Abd Allah ibn al-Harith ibn Juz'. Sahl is counted among the Successors by al-Bukhari, Abu Hatim, and everyone who mentioned him. The name is also rendered “Sahl ibn Tha'laba ibn Juz' al-Zubaydi.”

names.arabic: سهل بن ثعلبة بن جزء الزبيدي
names.english: Sahl ibn Tha'laba ibn Juz' al-Zubaydi

names.english: Abd Allah ibn al-Harith ibn Juz'

records.english: He is Ibn al-Hanzaliyyah; Abu Umar repeated him.

records.arabic: روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال تهادوا الحديث وعنه سعيد بن أبي هلال أورده أبو عمر قلت سهل تابعي أرسل وسعيد لم يلق أحدا من الصحابة
records.english: He related from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, who said, “Exchange gifts.” The rest of the hadith followed. Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal narrated from Sahl. Abu Umar listed him. I say: Sahl was a Successor whose report omits the Companion, and Sa'id did not meet any of the Companions.

records.arabic: كان اسمه حزنا أفرده بن منده عن سهل بن سعد فوهمه وبين ذلك أبو نعيم فأجاد
records.english: His name had been Hazn; Ibn Mandah listed him separately. He distinguished him from Sahl ibn Sa'd and was mistaken. Abu Nu'aym explained this well.

records.arabic: الجهني أورده بن شاهين في الصحابة وهو وهم نشأ عن سقط فإنه أخرج من طريق إسماعيل بن عباس عن أسيد بن عبد الرحمن عن فروة بن مجاهد عن سهل بن معاذ الجهني قال غزوت مع أبي الصائفة فنزلنا على حصن فضيق الناس المنازل وقطعوا الطرق فبعث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مناديا فنادى في الناس إن من ضيق منزلا أو قطع طريقا فلا جهاد له قلت لو تدبره بن شاهين لعلم وجه الوهم فإنه لم يكن في زمن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم صائفة وسبب هذا الوهم أنه سقط من المتن شيء وذلك واضح فيما أخرجه أحمد من طريق إسماعيل هذه بهذا الإسناد فقال فيه بعد قوله وقطعوا الطرق فقام معاذ بن أنس في الناس فقال أيها الناس أنا غزونا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم غزوة كذا فضيق الناس المنازل وقطعوا الطرق فبعث فذكره وهو عند أبي داود دون القصة وعنده من طريق الأوزاعي عن أسيد أيضا وأخرجه الطبراني من الوجهين وعند أبي يعلى من هذا الوجه عن سهل بن معاذ غزوت مع أبي الصائفة في زمن عبد الملك بن مروان وعلينا عبد الله بن عبد الملك فضيق الناس المنازل فقال معاذ أيها الناس إني غزوت مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فذكره فظهر أن الصحابي في هذا الحديث هو معاذ بن أنس لا ابنه سهل
records.english: Al-Juhani; Ibn Shahin included him among the Companions, but this is an error. The error was caused by an omission. He transmitted through Isma'il ibn Abbas, from Usayd ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Farwa ibn Mujahid, from Sahl ibn Mu'adh al-Juhani, who said: 'I went on a summer campaign with my father. We stopped by a fortress, and the people crowded the lodging places and blocked the roads. The Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم sent a herald, who called out to the people: "Whoever crowds a lodging place or blocks a road has no jihad."' I say: If Ibn Shahin had considered it, he would have known the cause of the error, for there were no such summer campaigns in the time of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. The error arose because part of the text was dropped. This is clear in Ahmad's transmission through this same route from Isma'il. After 'and blocked the roads,' it says: 'Then Mu'adh ibn Anas stood among the people and said, "People, we went on such-and-such a campaign with the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم, and the people crowded the lodging places and blocked the roads. So he sent..."' and then he quoted the report. Abu Dawud has it without the story, and also through al-Awza'i from Usayd. Al-Tabarani transmitted it through both routes. In Abu Ya'la's version through this route, Sahl ibn Mu'adh said: 'I went on a summer campaign with my father in the time of Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, with Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Malik commanding us. The people crowded the lodging places, so Mu'adh said, "People, I went on a campaign with the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم..."' and he cited the report. It is thus clear that the Companion in this hadith is Mu'adh ibn Anas, not his son Sahl.

records.arabic: ذكره الذهبي من مسند بقي فوهم فإنه من أتباع التابعين وقد تقدم حديثه في ترجمة سهل بن مالك وهو جده
records.english: Al-Dhahabi mentioned him from Baqi's Musnad, but he was mistaken. This was an error, for he belonged to the generation after the Successors. His hadith was previously mentioned in the biography of Sahl ibn Malik, his grandfather.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: غير منسوب ذكره الباوردي وأورد من طريق أبي حاتم أنه جلس إلى جنب إياس بن سهم فقال الا أحدثك عن أبي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كذا قال وإنما هو سهل باللام وقد أخرجه مطين بن محمد بن يزيد شيخ الباوردي فيه على الصواب وقد تقدم في أواخر من اسمه سهل مع الكلام عليه
records.english: No lineage is given. Al-Bawardi mentioned him. He transmitted through Abu Hatim that he sat beside Iyas ibn Sahm, who said, 'Shall I not tell you a report from my father, from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم?' This is how it was stated, but the name is actually Sahl, with a lam. Mutayyan ibn Muhammad ibn Yazid, al-Bawardi's teacher in this report, transmitted it correctly. It was previously mentioned near the end of those named Sahl, together with discussion of it.

records.arabic: المحاربي فرق بن شاهين بينه وبين سواء بن الحارث وهو هو
records.english: Al-Muharibi; Ibn Shahin distinguished him from Sawa' ibn al-Harith. They are the same man.

heading.english: The letter sin followed by waw

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: روى عنه أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن ذكره أبو عمر مغايرا لسواد بن عمرو وهو هو والعجب أنه نبه في ترجمة سواد بن عمرو على أنه يقال فيه بزيادة هاء وكأنه أشار إلى صنيع بن أبي حاتم فإنه ذكر سواد بن عمرو وفيمن اسمه سواد بلا هاء وذكر قصته في الخلوق وأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم طعنه في بطنه فسأله أن يقتص منه فكشف عن بطنه وشرع يقبله وذكر قبل ذلك فيمن اسمه سوادة بزيادة الهاء هذه القصة بعينها للسوادة بن عمرو وقال في كل منهما روى عنه الحسن البصري وكان ذكره قبل ذلك على صورة أخرى كما سأبينه في الذي بعده
records.english: Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman transmitted from him; Abu Umar mentioned him. Abu Umar treated him as someone distinct from Sawad ibn Amr, but they are the same man. It is strange that, in the biography of Sawad ibn Amr, Abu Umar noted that his name is also given with an added ha. He may have been referring to Ibn Abi Hatim's practice: Ibn Abi Hatim listed Sawad ibn Amr among those named Sawad, without a ha, and related his story concerning the perfume and how the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم prodded him in the stomach. Sawad asked for retaliation in kind, so the Prophet exposed his stomach and Sawad began to kiss it. Earlier, among those named Sawada with the added ha, Ibn Abi Hatim had given this very same story to Sawada ibn Amr. For each, he said that al-Hasan al-Basri narrated from him. He had earlier mentioned him in yet another form, as I shall explain in the next entry. The name is also rendered “Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman.”

records.arabic: تقدم في سواء بغير راء
records.english: He was discussed under Sawa', without the letter ra'.

records.arabic: ذكره بن أبي حاتم في أول من اسمه سوار بتشديد الواو وبعد الألف راء فقال بصري روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه نخسه بجريدة النخل فطالبه بالقصاص روى عنه الحسن البصري كذا قال وهو تصحيف شنيع لم يتابعه عليه بن عبد البر ولا غيره والصواب من هذا كله أن اسم الرجل سوادة بزيادة هاء وقد أشرت إلى ذلك في القسم الأول وسقت حديثه من عند البغوي في ترجمة سواد بن غزية لمعنى اقتضى ذلك
records.english: Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned him at the beginning of those named Sawwar, with a doubled waw. The name also has a ra after the alif, saying: 'A Basran. He narrated from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم that the Prophet poked him with a date-palm frond and that he demanded retaliation in kind. Al-Hasan al-Basri narrated from him.' That is what he said, but it is a grave misreading, followed by neither Ibn Abd al-Barr nor anyone else. The correct conclusion from all of this is that the man's name was Sawada, with an added ha. I referred to this in the first section and gave his hadith from al-Baghawi in the biography of Sawad ibn Ghaziya for a reason that called for doing so.

records.arabic: كذا وقع في بعض النسخ من الدارقطني والصواب سواد كما تقدم إيضاحه في القسم الأول
records.english: This is how he appears in some copies of al-Daraqutni; the correct form is Sawad. This was explained earlier in the first section. The name is also rendered “Ghaziya.”

records.arabic: أفرده أبو عمر ولم ينبه على أنه تقدم في سبيع
records.english: Abu Umar treated him separately and did not note that he appeared earlier under Subay'.

records.arabic: الفزاري ذكره أبو عمر الدمشقي في مسند الشاميين وهو غلط وليست له صحبة وحديثه مرسل قاله بن أبي حاتم وقال الدارقطني وابن منده لا يصح له صحبة وحديثه مرسل قلت له حديثان مرسلان أحدهما أخرجه البغوي وغيره من طريق الجراح بن مليح عن الزبيدي عن لقمان بن عامر عن سويد بن جبلة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لتزدحمن هذه الأمة على الحوض الحديث وأخرجه بن حبان في صحيحه والطبراني في مسند الشاميين من طريق عبد الله بن سالم عن الزبيدي بهذا الإسناد فقال عن سويد بن جبلة عن العرباض بن سارية وله عند الطبراني عن العرباض من هذا الوجه حديث آخر ومن هذا الوجه أيضا عنده عن عمرو بن عنبسة الحديث الثاني أخرجه بن شاهين وغيره من طريق بقية عن الزبيدي عن راشد بن سعد عن سويد بن جبلة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال العارية مؤداة الحديث وهذا أخرجه النسائي من طريق الحجاج بن فرافصة عن الزبيدي عن أبي عامر عنه عن أبي إمامة وهو الصواب
records.english: Al-Fazari; Abu Umar al-Dimashqi mentioned him in Musnad al-Shamiyyin. This is a mistake. He was not a Companion, and his hadith is mursal, according to Ibn Abi Hatim. Al-Daraqutni and Ibn Manda said that his status as a Companion is not established and that his hadith is mursal. I say: He has two mursal hadiths. The first was transmitted by al-Baghawi and others through al-Jarrah ibn Malih, from al-Zubaydi, from Luqman ibn Amir, from Suwayd ibn Jabala, from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, who said, 'This community will certainly crowd together at the Basin,' and the rest of the hadith. Ibn Hibban transmitted it in his Sahih, and al-Tabarani in Musnad al-Shamiyyin, through Abd Allah ibn Salim, from al-Zubaydi, with the same chain, but giving it as from Suwayd ibn Jabala, from al-Irbad ibn Sariya. Al-Tabarani also has another hadith from al-Irbad through this route, and a hadith through this route from Amr ibn Anbasa. The second hadith was transmitted by Ibn Shahin and others through Baqiyya, from al-Zubaydi, from Rashid ibn Sa'd, from Suwayd ibn Jabala, from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, who said, 'A borrowed article must be returned,' and the rest of the hadith. Al-Nasa'i transmitted this through al-Hajjaj ibn Furafisa, from al-Zubaydi, from Abu Amir, from him, from Abu Umama; the source does not identify the referent of 'him.' This is the route judged correct. The name is also rendered “Suwayd ibn Jabala al-Fazari.”

records.arabic: ذكره بن شاهين وساق الحديث الثاني في ترجمة الذي قبله فصحف أباه
records.english: Ibn Shahin mentioned him. He placed the second hadith from the preceding biography under his name, misreading his father's name.

records.arabic: بن خالد بن عقبة الأوسي ذكره بن شاهين وقال شك في إسلامه وقال أبو عمر أنا أشك فيه كما شك غيري ذكره بعضهم معتمدا على ما روى بن إسحاق عن عاصم بن عمرو عن أشياخ من قومه قالوا قدم سويد بن الصامت معتمرا فدعاه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى الإسلام فلم يبعد وقال إن هذا القول حسن ثم انصرف فقتل فكان رجال من قومه يقولون أنا لنراه مسلما قلت فإن صح ما قالوا لم يعد في الصحابة لأنه لم يلق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مؤمنا
records.english: Son of Khalid, son of Uqbah, al-Awsi. Ibn Shahin mentioned him and said that his acceptance of Islam is uncertain. Abu Umar said: 'I doubt it, as others do.' Some included him on the strength of Ibn Ishaq's narration from Asim ibn Amr, from elders of Suwayd's people. They said that Suwayd ibn al-Samit came to perform the minor pilgrimage, and the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم invited him to Islam. He did not reject it and said, 'This message is good.' He then departed and was killed. Some men of his people used to say, 'We think he was a Muslim.' I say: Even if what they said is sound, he is not counted among the Companions, because he did not meet the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم while he was a believer. The name is also rendered “Suwayd ibn al-Samit ibn Khalid ibn Uqba al-Awsi.”

names.arabic: سويد بن الصامت بن خالد بن عقبة الأوسي
names.english: Suwayd ibn al-Samit ibn Khalid ibn Uqba al-Awsi

records.arabic:
وقع ذكره في رسالة الغفران لأبي العلاء المعري بما يوهم أن له صحبه وليس كذلك فقال أبو العلاء ما نصه ولو أدرك سويد بن صبيع لشاغبه أيام الربيع وسويد هو الذي يقول
إذا طلبوا مني اليمن منحتهم
يمينا كبرد الأتحمي الممزق
وإن احلفوني بالطلاق أتيتها
على خير ما كنا ولم نتفرق
وإن احلفونى بالعتاق فقد درى
عبيد غلامي أنه غير معتق وكان يألف فراش سودة أم المؤمنين ويعرف مكانه الرسول ولا يتحرى عنه فسألني بعض المشايخ عن ترجمة سويد هذا وتوهم أنه صحابي لكنه لم يجد من يعرف بحاله وأنه كشف الاستيعاب وما استدرك عليه فلم يجد له ذكرا وكشف أنساب بني عامر بن لؤي رهط سودة فلم يذكروه فأجبته بان سويدا شاعر إسلامي وكان ماجنا وشعره يدل على كل من الأمرين المستتر والضمير في قول المعمري وكان ليس هو لسويد وإنما هو للذي خاطبه المعري بالرسالة المذكورة وإنه شرع بعد أن إجابة عن مراسلته له يمدحه ويصفه بأنه لو أدرك فلانا لعرفه ولو عاصر فلانا إلى غير ذلك حتى ذكر عددا من الناس لكنه اقتصر منهم على من يسمى الأسود أو من يشتق اسمه من السواد لأن لون الذي خاطبه كان إلى السواد أقرب فإذا تقرر هذا عرف أن الضمير في قوله وكان للمخاطب لا لسويد بن صبيع والله أعلم
records.english: He is mentioned in Abu al-Ala' al-Ma'arri's Epistle of Forgiveness. The passage suggests he was a Companion, but that is not so. Abu al-Ala said, verbatim: 'Had he encountered Suwayd ibn Subay', he would have disputed with him in the days of spring.' Suwayd is the man who said: 'If they ask me for al-yaman [the reading and sense of this word remain uncertain], I grant them / an oath like the torn cloak of al-Athami. / If they make me swear by divorce, I resort to it / though we are on the best terms and have not separated. / If they make me swear by manumission, / my slave Ubayd knows he is not freed.' 'He used to frequent the bed of Sawda, Mother of the Believers, and the Messenger knew where he was and did not seek him out.' A shaykh asked me about this Suwayd's biography, supposing him to be a Companion. He could find no one who knew his circumstances. He searched al-Isti'ab and its supplements without finding him mentioned, and examined the genealogies of Banu Amir ibn Lu'ayy, Sawda's clan, where they did not mention him either. I answered him that Suwayd was a poet of the Islamic period and was licentious; his poetry points to both traits. The canonical text places the word 'implicit' awkwardly after 'both,' although the following sentence discusses an implicit subject and pronoun. The source here calls the writer al-Ma'mari, apparently referring to al-Ma'arri named above. The implicit subject and pronoun in his words 'He used to...' do not refer to Suwayd. Rather, they refer to the person whom al-Ma'arri addressed in that letter. After answering his correspondent, al-Ma'arri began to praise and describe him, saying that had he met this person, he would have known him, and had he been a contemporary of that person, and so on, until he named a number of people. But he confined himself to people named al-Aswad or whose names derive from blackness, because the complexion of his addressee was closer to black. With this established, it is clear that the pronoun in 'He used to...' refers to the addressee, not to Suwayd ibn Subay'. والله أعلم

records.arabic: بن يزيد بن حارثة الأنصاري تابعي صغير لجده صحبة وأما هو فأخرج له البغوي وأبو يعلى من طريق مجمع بن يحيى قال سمعت سويد بن عامر أحد عمومتي قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بلوا أرحامكم ولو بالسلام قال بن حبان في ثقات التابعين حديثه مرسل وقال البغوي وابن منده لا صحبة له
records.english: Son of Yazid, son of Harithah, al-Ansari. He was a younger Successor. His grandfather was a Companion, but Suwayd was not. Al-Baghawi and Abu Ya'la transmitted through Mujamma' ibn Yahya, who said: 'I heard Suwayd ibn Amir, one of my paternal uncles, say: The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم said, "Refresh your ties of kinship, even if only with a greeting."' Ibn Hibban said in al-Thiqat al-Tabi'in that his hadith is mursal. Al-Baghawi and Ibn Manda said that he was not a Companion. The name is also rendered “Suwayd ibn Amir ibn Yazid ibn Haritha al-Ansari.”

names.arabic: سويد بن عامر بن يزيد بن حارثة الأنصاري
names.english: Suwayd ibn Amir ibn Yazid ibn Haritha al-Ansari

records.english: The father of Uqbah. Al-Baghawi distinguished him from Suwayd al-Ansari, but they are the same man: he was a Juhani allied with the Ansar.

records.english: Ibn Qani' mentioned him. According to this addition in al-Tajrid. But Ibn Qani' has only Siyaba, with an additional ba after the alif; that man was mentioned earlier in the first section.

records.arabic: ملك حمير ذكره بن منده في الصحابة وقال أدرك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأخبر جده عبد المطلب بنبوته وصفته ثم ساق في ترجمته حديث أنس أن ملك ذي يزن أهدى لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حلة قلت مات سيف قبل المبعث والذي أهدى إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وكاتبه ولده زرعة كما تقدم في ترجمته وروى بن هشام في الدفائن بسند منقطع عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن ظئره زوج حليمة أخبرهم إنهم لما أرادوا دفن سلول بن حبيشة وقفوا على باب مغلق فإذا فيه سرير عليه رجل وعند رأسه كتاب فيه أنا أبو شمر ذو النون فقال ذو النون هو سيف بن ذي يزن قلت وهو صريح في أنه مات قبل البعثة ولو كانوا يذكرون في الصحابة من فاه بذكر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ممن مات قبلهم للزمهم ذكر تبع ومسعر وسطيح وقس بن ساعدة وجمع كثير نحوهم هذا وفي آخر الجزء الأول من النسخة ب هنا آخر المجلد الأول من كتاب الإصابة في أسماء الصحابة لشيخ الإسلام قاضي القضاة أبي الفضل بن حجر الكناني العسقلاني أمتع الله المسلمين ببقائه وادام علومه في معالي ارتقائه آمين آمين آمين يتلوه إن شاء الله تعالى في أول المجلد الثاني حرف الشين المعجمة القسم الأول والحمد الله أولا وآخرا ظاهرا وباطنا حسبنا الله ونعم الوكيل وصلى الله على سيدنا محمدا وآله وصحبه وسلم تسليما أبدا إلى يوم الدين ووافق الفراغ من تعليقه يوم الأحد 13 جمادى الأول سنة 842 أحسن الله العواقب بمنه وكرمه آمين والحمد لله رب العالمين ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله العظيم وأمامه في الهامش مدرت على هذا الجزء من أوله إلى آخره كتبه علي الحلبي الشافعي عفى عنه
records.english: The king of Himyar; Ibn Mandah included him among the Companions. Ibn Mandah said that he lived in the Prophet's صلى الله عليه وسلم time and informed the Prophet's grandfather Abd al-Muttalib of his future prophethood and description. Ibn Manda then gave under his biography Anas's hadith that the king of Dhi Yazan presented the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم with a robe. I say: Sayf died before the Prophet's mission. The person who presented a gift to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم and corresponded with him was Sayf's son Zur'a, as noted in his biography. Ibn Hisham narrated in al-Dafa'in, with a broken chain, from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم that his foster father, Halima's husband, told them that when they wished to bury Salul ibn Hubaysha, they stopped at a locked door. Inside was a couch with a man upon it, and at his head a writing that said, 'I am Abu Shamir Dhu al-Nun.' He said: Dhu al-Nun is Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan. I say: This clearly shows that he died before the prophetic mission. If they were to include among the Companions anyone who spoke of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم but died before the mission, they would have to include Tubba', Mis'ar, Satih, Quss ibn Sa'ida, and many others like them. Now, at the end of the first part of copy B, there is this note: 'Here ends the first volume of Al-Isabah fi Asma al-Sahaba, by the Shaykh al-Islam, Chief Judge Abu al-Fadl Ibn Hajar al-Kinani al-Asqalani. May God grant the Muslims enjoyment through his continued life and perpetuate his learning in the lofty heights of his advancement. Amen, amen, amen. Next, إن شاء الله تعالى, at the beginning of the second volume, is the dotted letter shin, the first section. Praise be to God at the beginning and the end, outwardly and inwardly. God is sufficient for us and the best trustee. May God bless our master Muhammad, his family, and his Companions, and grant them peace forever, until the Day of Judgment. The copying was completed on Sunday, the thirteenth of Jumada al-Ula in the year 842. May God, by His favor and generosity, grant good outcomes. Amen. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. There is no power or strength except through God, the Magnificent.' Before it, in the margin, is written: '[an unclear verb] this part from beginning to end. Written by Ali al-Halabi al-Shafi'i. May He pardon him.'

names.english: Abu al-Fadl Ibn Hajar al-Kinani al-Asqalani

records.english: One of the jinn who embraced Islam. He was mentioned earlier in the biography of al-Arqam.

heading.english: The letter shin followed by alif)

records.arabic:
من الجن وقع ذكره في خبر غريب لسعد بن عبادة أخرجه الزبير بن بكار في الموفقيات قال حدثنا الرياشي سمعت سليمان بن عبد العزيز بن أبي ثابت يحدث قال حدثني أبي عن عبد الحميد بن بهرام عن شهر بن حوشب عن بن عباس عن سعد بن عبادة قال بعثني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى حضرموت في حاجة له وهو بمكة فلما كنت ببعض الطريق عرست في الليل فسمعت هاتفا يقول
أبا عمرو تأوبني السهود
وراح النوم وامتنع الهجود فذكر أبياتا قال فناداه هاتف آخر فقال يا زلعب ذهب بك العجب إن أعجب العجب بين مكة ويثرب قال وماذا يا شاصر قال نبي أرسل بخير الكلام إلى جميع الأنام يخرج من بين البلد الحرام إلى نخيل وآطام فقال آخر ما هذا النبي المرسل والكتاب المنزل قال رجل من لؤي بن غالب فذكر القصة إلى أن قال فسمعت صيحة كأنها صيحة حبلى فطلع الفجر فرأيت عظاية وثعبانا ميتين فقدمت فإذا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قد هاجر إلى المدينة
records.english: One of the jinn. He is mentioned in an unusual account from Sa'd ibn Ubada, transmitted by al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar in al-Muwaffaqiyyat. He said: Al-Riyashi told us, 'I heard Sulayman ibn Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Thabit narrate: My father told me, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Ibn Abbas, from Sa'd ibn Ubada, who said: "The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم sent me on an errand to Hadramawt while he was in Mecca. When I reached a place along the way, I stopped to rest at night and heard a disembodied voice say: 'Abu Amr, wakefulness has come over me; / sleep has gone away and slumber has been denied.'"' He mentioned further verses. Sa'd said: 'Another disembodied voice called to him, "Zal'ab, wonder has overcome you! The greatest wonder lies between Mecca and Yathrib." He said, "What is it, Shasir?" The voice said, "A prophet sent with the best of speech to all humankind, who will go forth from the Sacred City to date palms and fortified dwellings." Another said, "Who is this sent prophet, and what is this revealed book?" He said, "A man of Lu'ayy ibn Ghalib."' He continued the story until he said: 'I heard a scream like that of a pregnant woman. Dawn broke, and I saw a lizard and a snake, both dead. I arrived and found that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم had migrated to Medina.'

names.arabic: سليمان بن عبد العزيز بن أبي ثابت
names.english: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Thabit

records.arabic: بن عبيد بن عبد يزيد بن هاشم بن المطلب المطلبي جد الإمام الشافعي تقدم ذكره في ترجمة أبيه غير مسمى وذكر الخطيب في تاريخه أنه سمع أبا الطيب طاهر بن عبد الله الطبري يقول شافع بن السائب الذي ينسب إليه الإمام الشافعي قد لقي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو مترعرع وأسلم أبوه يوم بدر وسيأتي له ذكر في ترجمة عبد يزيد والد جده
records.english: Son of Ubayd, son of Abd Yazid, son of Hashim, son of al-Muttalib, al-Muttalibi. The grandfather of Imam al-Shafi'i. He was mentioned previously in his father's biography without being named. Al-Khatib said in his History that he heard Abu al-Tayyib Tahir ibn Abd Allah al-Tabari say: Shafi' ibn al-Sa'ib, after whom Imam al-Shafi'i is named, met the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم as a growing youth, and his father accepted Islam on the day of Badr. He will also be mentioned in the biography of Abd Yazid, the father of his grandfather. The name is also rendered “Shafi' ibn al-Sa'ib ibn Ubayd ibn Abd Yazid ibn Hashim ibn al-Muttalib al-Muttalibi.”

names.arabic: شافع بن السائب بن عبيد بن عبد يزيد بن هاشم بن المطلب المطلبي
names.english: Shafi' ibn al-Sa'ib ibn Ubayd ibn Abd Yazid ibn Hashim ibn al-Muttalib al-Muttalibi

names.arabic: أبا الطيب طاهر بن عبد الله الطبري
names.english: Abu al-Tayyib Tahir ibn Abd Allah al-Tabari

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: روى بن أبي شيبة بإسناد حسن لكنه مرسل عن أبي سلمة ويحيى بن عبد الرحمن قالا كانت بين رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وبين المشركين هدنة فذكر حديثا طويلا وفيه فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم وهي ساعتي هذه حرام لا يعضد شجرها فقال له رجل يقال له شاو والناس يقولون قال العباس يا رسول الله إلا الإذخر الحديث قلت والذي ثبت في الصحيحين أيضا أن القائل هو العباس ولولا أن الراوي مثبت لهذا الاسم لكتبته في الأوهام وقد أخرج أبو موسى من طريق أبي سلمة عن أبي هريرة في هذا لحديث فقال شاه اليماني اكتب لي وهذا وهم وإنما هو أبو شاه كما سيأتي في الكنى
records.english: Ibn Abi Shaybah transmitted it with a good chain, although it is mursal. The report came from Abu Salama and Yahya ibn Abd al-Rahman, who said: There was a truce between the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم and the polytheists. They then related a long hadith, which includes: The Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم said, 'This town is sacred from this very hour of mine; its trees are not to be cut.' A man called Shaw said to him—though people say that it was al-Abbas—'Messenger of God, except the idhkhir grass,' and the rest of the hadith. I say: The two Sahih collections also establish that the speaker was al-Abbas. Were it not that the narrator explicitly gave this name, I would have placed it among the errors. Abu Musa transmitted through Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra, in this hadith the words 'Shah al-Yamani said: Write it for me.' This is an error: he is Abu Shah, as will appear among the kunyas.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن سلامة بن أوس بن عمرو بن كعب البلوي حليف الأنصار تقدم ذكر أبيه قال بن سعد شهد خديج وزوجه أم منيع بنت عمرو بن عدي بن سنان العقبة وولدت شباثا ليلة العقبة وشباث ضبطه بن ماكولا بضم أوله أوله وتخفيف ثانيه وآخره مثلثة وقال بن أبي حاتم عن أبيه لا يعرف وقال أبو عمر ليست له رواية
records.english: Son of Salamah, son of Aws, son of Amr, son of Ka'b, al-Balawi, an ally of the Ansar. His father was mentioned previously. Ibn Sa'd said that Khadij and his wife Umm Mani' bint Amr ibn Adi ibn Sinan attended the pledge at al-Aqaba, and she bore Shubath on the night of al-Aqaba. Ibn Makula vocalized Shubath with a damma on its first letter, a light second letter, and a tha as its last letter. Ibn Abi Hatim reported from his father: 'He is not known.' Abu Umar said that no narration from him is known. The name is also rendered “Shubath ibn Khadij ibn Salama ibn Aws ibn Amr ibn Ka'b al-Balawi.”

names.arabic: شباث بن خديج بن سلامة بن أوس بن عمرو بن كعب البلوي
names.english: Shubath ibn Khadij ibn Salama ibn Aws ibn Amr ibn Ka'b al-Balawi

names.arabic: أم منيع بنت عمرو بن عدي بن سنان
names.english: Umm Mani' bint Amr ibn Adi ibn Sinan

heading.english: The letter shin followed by ba

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن مالك البلوي قال بن يونس له صحبة وشهد فتح مصر وله ذكر في كتاب الفتوح وقال يحيى بن عثمان بن صالح عن بن عفير شهد بيعة الرضوان وفتح مصر ولا يحفظ له رواية كذا قال وقد أخرج بن منده من طريق أحمد بن سيار بسند فيه بن لهيعة عن شبث بن سعد أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال إن العبد ليخرج له يوم القيامة كتاب فيه حسنات الحديث وأخرجه أبو نعيم في الصحابة أيضا ومن طريقه أبو منصور الديلمي في مسند الفردوس وشبث ضبطه بن ماكولا بفتح أوله وثانيه وآخره مثلثة وقيل هو بكسر أوله وسكون التحتانية ثم مثلثة فالله أعلم
records.english: Son of Malik, al-Balawi. Ibn Yunus said that he was a Companion, witnessed the conquest of Egypt, and is mentioned in the Book of Conquests. Yahya ibn Uthman ibn Salih reported from Ibn Ufair that he attended the Pledge of Ridwan and the conquest of Egypt, but no narration from him is known. So he said. Yet Ibn Manda transmitted through Ahmad ibn Sayyar, with a chain containing Ibn Lahi'a, from Shabath ibn Sa'd, that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم said: 'A servant will indeed have brought forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a record containing good deeds,' and the rest of the hadith. Abu Nu'aym also included it in his work on the Companions, and through him Abu Mansur al-Daylami included it in Musnad al-Firdaws. Ibn Makula vocalized Shabath with fatha on its first and second letters and a tha at the end. It is also said to have a kasra on its first letter, then a still ya, then tha. The name is also rendered “Shabath ibn Sa'd ibn Malik al-Balawi.” And الله أعلم.

names.arabic: شبث بن سعد بن مالك البلوي
names.english: Shabath ibn Sa'd ibn Malik al-Balawi

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بفتح أوله وثانيه وقال بن ماكولا بسكون ثانيه بن صعفوق بفاء وقاف وزن عصفور قال أبو موسى وجدته بقافين وقال أبو نصر صعفوق بفتح أوله ولم يأت على هذا الوزن غيره إلا خرنوب مع أن الفصحاء يضمون أوله قال أبو أحمد الحاكم في ترجمة أبي عبيد السري بن يحيى أن جده شبر بن صعفوق بن عمرو الكاتب بن زرارة بن عدس بن زيد بن عبد الله بن دارم التميمي الدارمي وفد على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأمره على صدقة قومه
records.english: With fatha on its first and second letters. Ibn Makula said that the second has a sukun. He was the son of Sa'fuq, written with fa and qaf and on the pattern of usfur. Abu Musa said: I found it written with two qafs. Abu Nasr said: Sa'fuq has a fatha on its first letter. No other name on this pattern occurs, except kharnub, though eloquent speakers give the latter a damma on its first letter. Abu Ahmad al-Hakim said in the biography of Abu Ubayd al-Sari ibn Yahya that the latter's grandfather was Shabar ibn Sa'fuq ibn Amr al-Katib ibn Zurara ibn Adas ibn Zayd ibn Abd Allah ibn Darim al-Tamimi al-Darimi. He came as a delegate to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, who placed him in charge of collecting the alms tax of his people.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: غير منسوب وقع ذكره في حديث صحيح فروى أبو داود وأحمد وإسحاق وأبو يعلى والدارقطني والطبراني من طريق عزرة بن ثابت عن سعيد بن جبير عن بن عباس قال سمع صلى الله عليه وسلم رجلا يلبي عن شبرمة فقال أحججت قال لا قال هذه عن نفسك وحج عن شبرمة وروى الدارقطني من طريق عمرو بن دينار عن عطاء عن بن عباس نحوه ورواه الدارقطني من طريق أبي الزبير عن جابر من طريق عطاء عن عائشة نحوه
records.english: No lineage is given; he is mentioned in a sound report. Abu Dawud, Ahmad, Ishaq, Abu Ya'la, al-Daraqutni, and al-Tabarani transmitted through Azra ibn Thabit, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم heard a man pronouncing the pilgrimage talbiya on behalf of Shubruma. He asked, 'Have you performed the pilgrimage yourself?' The man said, 'No.' He said, 'Perform this one for yourself, and then perform the pilgrimage for Shubruma.' Al-Daraqutni narrated something similar through Amr ibn Dinar, from Ata', from Ibn Abbas, and likewise through Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, and through Ata', from A'isha.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: المزني جاء عنه حديثان أحدهما في قصة العسيف والآخر في قصة الأمة إذا زنت قال بن السكن الاختلاف فيه عن الزهري فالأكثر قالوا عنه عن عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن عتبة عن أبي هريرة وزيد بن خالد وابن عتبة مثلهم لكن زاد وشبل غير منسوب وشعيب وبكر بن وائل عن عمرو بن شعيب وعبيد الله بن أبي زياد قالوا عن أبي هريرة فقط قال وجاء يونس بالحديث على وجهه فقال عن الزهري عن عبيد الله عن شبل بن عامر المزني عن عبد الله بن مالك الأوسي ووافقه الزبيدي وابن أخي الزهري في السند لكن قالا شبل بن خليد قال بن حبان له صحبة ومن زعم أنه شبل بن حامد فقد وهم وقال في التابعين شبل بن خليد روى عن عبد الله بن مالك الأوسي وهذا هو شبل بن خليد الذي ذكره قبل وقيل فيه شبل بن حامد واشتبه أمره على بن حبان وبقي من وجوه الاختلاف فيه رواية عقيل فقال عن الزهري عن عبد الله عن شبل وخليد عن مالك بن عبد الله الأوسي قال بن السكن شبل يقال له صحبة وكان بن عيينة يخطىء فيه فيقول شبل بن معبد قال والصواب أنه شبل بن حامد وأنه يروي عن عبد الله بن مالك الأوسي قلت وهو غير شبل بن معبد البجلي الآتي في القسم الثالث
records.english: Al-Muzani; two reports have come from him. Hadiths are attributed to him, one concerning the hired laborer and the other concerning a slave woman who commits fornication. Ibn al-Sakan said that the narrations from al-Zuhri differ. Most narrators gave it from him, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Utba, from Abu Hurayra and Zayd ibn Khalid. Ibn Utba gave it similarly but added Shibl without a lineage. Shu'ayb, Bakr ibn Wa'il, Amr ibn Shu'ayb, and Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad gave it from Abu Hurayra alone; the source's intervening 'from' does not make their precise linkage clear. Ibn al-Sakan said: Yunus transmitted the hadith in its proper form, from al-Zuhri, from Ubayd Allah, from Shibl ibn Amir al-Muzani, from Abd Allah ibn Malik al-Awsi. Al-Zubaydi and al-Zuhri's nephew agreed with him on the chain, but called the man Shibl ibn Khulayd. Ibn Hibban said that he was a Companion and that anyone who claimed he was Shibl ibn Hamid had erred. Yet among the Successors Ibn Hibban listed Shibl ibn Khulayd as narrating from Abd Allah ibn Malik al-Awsi. This is the same Shibl ibn Khulayd whom he had mentioned earlier; he is also called Shibl ibn Hamid, and Ibn Hibban confused his identity. Another of the divergent versions remains: Uqayl narrated from al-Zuhri, from Abd Allah, from Shibl and Khulayd, from Malik ibn Abd Allah al-Awsi. Ibn al-Sakan said: Shibl is said to have been a Companion. Ibn Uyayna used to err concerning him and say Shibl ibn Ma'bad. Ibn al-Sakan said: The correct name is Shibl ibn Hamid, and he narrated from Abd Allah ibn Malik al-Awsi. I say: He is distinct from Shibl ibn Ma'bad al-Bajali, who will appear in the third section.

names.arabic: عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن عتبة
names.english: Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Utba

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن مهان بن وهب بن لقيط بن يعمر الشداخ الكناني الليثي شهد الحديبية قاله بن الكلبي والطبري واستدركه بن فتحون وابن الأثير
records.english: Son of Mahan, son of Wahb, son of Laqit, son of Ya'mur, al-Shaddakh al-Kinani al-Laythi. He attended al-Hudaybiya, according to Ibn al-Kalbi and al-Tabari. Ibn Fathun and Ibn al-Athir added him. The name is also rendered “Shabib ibn Haram ibn Mahan ibn Wahb ibn Laqit ibn Ya'mur al-Shaddakh al-Kinani al-Laythi.”

names.arabic: شبيب بن حرام بن مهان بن وهب بن لقيط بن يعمر الشداخ الكناني الليثي
names.english: Shabib ibn Haram ibn Mahan ibn Wahb ibn Laqit ibn Ya'mur al-Shaddakh al-Kinani al-Laythi

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن أسيد الكندي له صحبة ذكره بن منده وأخرج له من طريق شبيب بن حبيب بن غالب عن عمه شبيب بن غالب عن أبيه غالب بن أسيد عن أبيه أسيد بن شيب عن أبيه أنه سأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن المسح على الخفين وفي سنده على بن قرين وهو واه
records.english: Son of Usayd, al-Kindi. He was a Companion, according to Ibn Manda, who transmitted through Shabib ibn Habib ibn Ghalib, from his paternal uncle Shabib ibn Ghalib, from his father Ghalib ibn Usayd, from his father Usayd ibn Shayb, from his father, that he asked the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم about wiping over leather socks. Ali ibn Qurayn is in its chain, and he is weak. The name is also rendered “Shabib ibn Ghalib ibn Usayd al-Kindi.”

names.arabic: شبيب بن غالب بن أسيد الكندي
names.english: Shabib ibn Ghalib ibn Usayd al-Kindi

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: أو بن أبي مرثد الغساني له ذكر في حديث أخرجه الحارث بن أسامة من طريق المسور بن عبد الله الباهلي عن بعض ولد الجارود أنه أخذ هذه النسخة من نسخة عهد العلاء بن الحضرمي حين بعثه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى البحرين وشهده معاوية وعثمان والمختار بن قيس وقصي بن أبي عميرة وفي رواية بن أبي عمرو وسعد بن عبادة والضحاك بن أبي عمرو وشبيب بن أبي مرثد وفي رواية بن قرة والمستنير بن أبي صعصعة الخزاعي وعوانه أو عبادة بن الشماخ الجهني وسعد بن مالك وسعد بن معاذ وزيد بن عمير وفي رواية يزيد بن عميرة وزاد في رواية ونوفل بن طلحة وسيأتي له سياق آخر في ترجمة عوانة بن الشماخ إن شاء الله تعالى
records.english: Or son of Abi Marthad, al-Ghassani. He is mentioned in a hadith transmitted by al-Harith ibn Usama through al-Miswar ibn Abd Allah al-Bahili, from one of the descendants of al-Jarud, who took this copy from a copy of the covenant of al-Ala ibn al-Hadrami when the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم sent him to Bahrain. Its witnesses were Mu'awiya, Uthman, al-Mukhtar ibn Qays, and Qusayy ibn Abi Umayra—or, in another version, Ibn Abi Amr—as well as Sa'd ibn Ubada, al-Dahhak ibn Abi Amr, Shabib ibn Abi Marthad—or, in another version, Ibn Qurra—al-Mustanir ibn Abi Sa'sa'a al-Khuza'i, Awana or Ubada ibn al-Shammakh al-Juhani, Sa'd ibn Malik, Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, and Zayd ibn Umayr—or, in another version, Yazid ibn Umayra. Another version adds Nawfal ibn Talha. Another wording of this report will appear in the biography of Awana ibn al-Shammakh, إن شاء الله تعالى.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: أورده الطبراني من طريق بقية عن أبي بكر بن أبي مريم عن راشد بن سعد عن شبيب بن نعيم أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال أم ملدم تأكل اللحم وتشرب الدم بردها وحرها من جهنم وقال البخاري في تاريخه شبيب بن نعيم أبو روح الحمصي روى عنه عبد الملك بن عمير فما أدري هو ذا أو غيره وأبو روح تابعي لا صحبة له وسيأتي في القسم الأخير
records.english: Al-Tabarani included him. The report came through Baqiyya, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Maryam, from Rashid ibn Sa'd, from Shabib ibn Nu'aym, that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم said: 'Umm Mildam eats flesh and drinks blood. Its cold and its heat come from Hell.' Al-Bukhari said in his History: 'Shabib ibn Nu'aym Abu Ruh al-Himsi; Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr narrated from him.' I do not know whether this is the same man or another. Abu Ruh was a Successor and not a Companion; he will appear in the final section.

records.arabic: يأتي في المبهمات
records.english: He will appear among the unidentified persons. The name is also rendered “Shabīb.”

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بالتصغير ذكره أبو القاسم البغوي وقال أحسبه سكن المدينة وأخرج من طريق إبراهيم بن جعفر عن سعيد بن شتيم أحد بني سهم بن مرة حدثه أبوه أنه كان في جيش عيينة بن حصن لما جاء يمد يهود خيبر قال فسمعنا صوتا في عسكر عيينة أيها الناس أهلكم خولفتم إليهم قال فرجعوا لا يتناظرون فلم ير لذلك نبأ وما نراه كان إلا من السماء وأورده أبو نعيم في ترجمة شنتم والد عاصم الآتي وهو خطأ وفرق بينهما البغوي والحسين بن علي البرديجي وجعفر المستغفري وغيرهم وذكر بن الأمين أن بن الفرضي قال وجدته مضبوطا عن الصنابحي عن البغوي بفتح أوله وكسر ثانيه قلت والذي عندنا في النسخ المعتمدة من كتاب البغوي بصيغة التصغير كما ذكرته
records.english: In the diminutive form; Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi mentioned him. He said, “I think he lived in Medina.” He transmitted, by way of Ibrāhīm ibn Jaʿfar, from Saʿīd ibn Shutaym, one of the descendants of Sahm ibn Murra, who was told by his father that he had been in ʿUyayna ibn Ḥiṣn’s army when ʿUyayna came to reinforce the Jews of Khaybar. He said: “We heard a voice in ʿUyayna’s camp: ‘People, your families! Others have gone to them while you are away.’ They turned back at once, without waiting for one another. No report of any such event was found, and we think the voice could only have come from heaven.” Abū Nuʿaym included this under Shantam, the father of ʿĀṣim who appears below, but that is an error. Al-Baghawī, al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī al-Bardījī, Jaʿfar al-Mustaghfirī, and others distinguished the two. Ibn al-Amīn reported that Ibn al-Faraḍī said: “I found it vocalized, through al-Ṣanābiḥī from al-Baghawī, with a fatḥa on its first letter and a kasra on its second.” I say: in the reliable copies of al-Baghawī’s book that we have, it is in the diminutive form, as I have stated.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بتخفيف الجيم السلفي بضم المهملة ذكره العسكري في الصحابة وقال أبو حاتم روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم روى عنه أبو عيسى وأخشى أن يكون حديثه مرسلا وكذا قال أبو عمر وأورده بن قافع من طريق الحسن قال حدثني رجل من بني سليط يقال له شجار أنه مر على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو جالس على باب المسجد وهو يقول المسلم أخو المسلم الحديث قلت فإحدى النسبتين تصحيف والأصوب الثاني فهو السليطي
records.english: With an undoubled jim; al-Sulafi has a damma on the sin. The jim is undotted. Al-ʿAskarī mentioned him among the Companions. Abū Ḥātim said: “He transmitted from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, and Abū ʿĪsā transmitted from him; I fear that his report is disconnected.” Abū ʿUmar said the same. Ibn Qāniʿ included him through al-Ḥasan, who said: “A man of Banū Sulayṭ called Shujār told me that he passed the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم while he was sitting at the mosque door and saying, ‘A Muslim is a Muslim’s brother,’” and he related the rest of the report. I say: one of the two tribal designations is a copyist’s error, and the second is more likely correct; thus he is al-Sulayṭī.

records.arabic:
السدوسي روى بن أبي خيثمة وعبد بن حميد في التفسير وأبو مسلم الكجي كلهم من طريق العباس بن خليس عن عكرمة قال أن هذه الآية في النساء والمحصنات من النساء نزلت في امرأة يقال لها معاذة كانت تحت شيخ من بني سدوس يقال له شجاع بن الحارس وكان معه ضرة لها ولدت لشجاع أولادا وأن شجاعا انطلق يمير أهله من هجر فمر بمعاذة بن عم لها فقالت له احملني إلى أهلي فرجع الشيخ فلم يجدها فانطلق إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فشكا إليه وأنشده
يا ملك الناس وديان العرب
الأبيات فقال انطلقوا فإن وجدتم الرجل كشف لها ثوبا فارجموها وإلا فردوا إلى الشيخ امرأته قال فانطلق بن ضرتها مالك بن شجاع بن الحارث فجاء بها فلما أشرف على الحي استقبلته أم مالك ترميها بالحجارة وتقول لابنها يا ضار أمه قال فلما نزلت معاذة واطمأنت جعل شجاع يقول
لعمري ما حبي معاذة بالذي
يغيره الواشي ولا قدم العهد قلت وقد وقع نحو ذلك للأعشى المازني كما تقدم في الهمزة
records.english: Al-Sadusi; Ibn Abi Khaythamah transmitted it. ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd in his Tafsīr and Abū Muslim al-Kajjī also transmitted through al-ʿAbbās ibn Khulays, from ʿIkrima, who said: “This verse concerning women, ‘and married women among women,’ was revealed about a woman called Muʿādha. She was married to an old man of Banū Sadūs called Shujāʿ ibn al-Ḥāris. He had another wife, who had borne Shujāʿ children. Shujāʿ went to Hajar to obtain provisions for his family. A paternal cousin of Muʿādha passed by her, and she said to him, ‘Take me to my family.’ The old man returned and did not find her, so he went to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, complained to him, and recited to him: ‘O king of the people and judge of the Arabs ...,’” followed by the verses. He said: “Go. If you find that the man has uncovered a garment for her, stone her; otherwise return the old man’s wife to him.” The son of her co-wife, Mālik ibn Shujāʿ ibn al-Ḥārith, went and brought her back. When he came into view of the settlement, Mālik’s mother met him, throwing stones at Muʿādha and saying to her son, “O you who would harm his mother!” Once Muʿādha had dismounted and settled, Shujāʿ began to say: “By my life, my love for Muʿādha is not such / as a slanderer or the passing of time could change.” I say: something similar happened to al-Aʿshā al-Māzinī, as mentioned earlier under alif. The name is also rendered “Ibn Abī Khaythama.”

records.arabic: ويقال بن أبي وهب بن ربيعة بن أسد بن صهيب بن مالك بن كبير بن غنم بن دودان بن أسد بن خزيمة الأسدي ذكره بن إسحاق في السابقين الأولين وفيمن هاجر إلى الحبشة وفيمن شهد بدرا وكذا ذكره موسى بن عقبة وابن الكلبي وعروة وقال بن أبي حاتم شجاع بن وهب أخو عقبة من المهاجرين الأولين وروى الطبراني من حديث المسور بن مخرمة قال بعث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم شجاع بن وهب الأسدي إلى المنذر بن الحارث بن أبي شمر الغساني وذكر بن سعد عن الواقدي بأسانيده أنه بعثه إلى الحارث بن أبي شمر وروى بن وهب عن يونس عن الزهري عن حميد بن عبد الرحمن عن شجاع بن وهب أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعثه إلى جبلة وكذا قال الواقدي عن شمر عن الزهري ورواه بن منده من طريق بريدة بن الحصيب نحوه وقال بن سعد وابن الكلبي وغيرهما استشهد باليمامة وكنيته أبو وهب
records.english: He is also said to be son of Abi Wahb. His lineage continues through Rabīʿa ibn Asad ibn Ṣuhayb ibn Mālik ibn Kabīr ibn Ghanm ibn Dūdān ibn Asad ibn Khuzayma al-Asadī. Ibn Isḥāq named him among the earliest believers, among those who emigrated to Abyssinia, and among those who witnessed Badr. Mūsā ibn ʿUqba, Ibn al-Kalbī, and ʿUrwa likewise named him. Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: “Shujāʿ ibn Wahb, brother of ʿUqba, was among the earliest Emigrants.” Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted from al-Miswar ibn Makhrama that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم sent Shujāʿ ibn Wahb al-Asadī to al-Mundhir ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Abī Shamir al-Ghassānī. Ibn Saʿd, through al-Wāqidī with his chains, stated that he sent him to al-Ḥārith ibn Abī Shamir. Ibn Wahb transmitted from Yūnus, from al-Zuhrī, from Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Shujāʿ ibn Wahb, that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم sent him to Jabala. Al-Wāqidī, from Shamir, from al-Zuhrī, said the same. Ibn Manda transmitted something similar through Burayda ibn al-Ḥuṣayb. Ibn Saʿd, Ibn al-Kalbī, and others said that he was martyred at al-Yamāma and that his kunya was Abū Wahb.

names.arabic: المنذر بن الحارث بن أبي شمر
names.english: al-Mundhir ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Abī Shamir

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بالنون شهد حنينا مع هوازن فلما انهزموا جاء فأسلم وقال للمسلمين أين الخيل البلق والرجال الذين عليهم الثياب البيض ما كنا نراكم فيهم إلا كالشامة قالوا تلك الملائكة ذكره الأموي في مغازيه واستدركه بن فتحون
records.english: With nun; he took part at Hunayn with Hawazin. When they were defeated, he came and accepted Islam, and said to the Muslims: “Where are the piebald horses and the men in white clothes? Among them, we could see you only as a small mark.” They said: “Those were the angels.” Al-Umawī mentioned him in his Maghāzī, and Ibn Fatḥūn added him as an omitted entry. The names in this notice are also rendered “Shajara al-Naṣrī” and “Hawāzin.”

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ذكره يحيى بن منده مستدركا على جده وقال سعيد بن يعقوب الأصبهاني لا أدري له صحبة أم لا وروى أحمد بن يونس الضبي من طريق خالد بن طهمان عن شجرة الكندي قال شهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم جنازة فأثنى الناس عليها خيرا فجلس وهو يدفن فأتاه جبريل فقال إن هذا الرجل ليس كما اثنوا عليه وإن الله قبل شهادتهم وغفر له ما لا يعلمون
records.english: Yahya ibn Mandah added him. Yahya added him to his grandfather’s work and said: “Saʿīd ibn Yaʿqūb al-Iṣbahānī said, ‘I do not know whether he was a Companion.’” Aḥmad ibn Yūnus al-Ḍabbī transmitted through Khālid ibn Ṭahmān from Shajara al-Kindī, who said: “The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم attended a funeral. The people spoke well of the deceased, and he sat while the man was buried. Gabriel came to him and said, ‘This man is not as they have praised him, but God has accepted their testimony and forgiven him what they do not know.’” The name is also rendered “Yaḥyā ibn Manda.”

records.arabic: الليثي هو بن الهاد يأتي
records.english: Al-Laythi; he is Ibn al-Had, to be discussed later. The names in this notice are also rendered “Shaddād ibn Usāma”, “Usāma”, and “Ibn al-Hād.”

records.arabic: بن شعوب يأتي
records.english: Son of Sha'ub; he will appear later. The names in this notice are also rendered “Shaddād ibn al-Aswad” and “Shaʿūb.”
